answer: Tie voting power to a work ledger that grows only from verified jobs. A newcomer registers, then completes three audited, client-signed tasks in fourteen days. Job credits decay ten percent weekly, so idle identities lose influence. A farmer chasing 1,000 voting agents must forge 3,000 signed records and spend about $180,000 in fees and wages across a fortnight of audits. The delta between one real worker and a thousand puppets stays visible, and one fraud report sends a ripple through the fake network as linked credits freeze. Trust is steel tempered by repeated heat and testing.
